final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced on 9.12.0 only (already fixed). The bug also shows up on 9.13.0 and 9.14.0. The checkout is 9.15.0 (`6f37b07`), and there the reporter's snippet doesn't fail.

**Expected:** The autofix keeps the outer `else` unreachable.

**Actual (9.12.0–9.14.0):** The rule reports `4:9 Unexpected if as the only statement in an else block.` and the fix turns `else { if (false) {} }` into `else if (false) {}`. After that, the outer `else` belongs to the new `if (false)`. I ran both versions in `node:vm`: the original code runs fine, and the fixed code throws `This \`else\` should have been unreachable!`.

**At the checkout (9.15.0):** There's no message and no fix, and the code runs the same before and after.

**Trigger:** An `else { if (x) ... }` block whose inner `if` has no `else`, inside an `if` that has no braces and has its own `else`. Once the block's braces are removed, that outer `else` attaches to the inner `if`.

**Likely cause:** In 9.14.0, the rule (`lib/rules/no-lonely-if.js`) reports any single-statement `else` block. 9.15.0 adds `!astUtils.areBracesNecessary(parent, sourceCode)` to the report condition (lib/rules/no-lonely-if.js lines 44-47). This is the same helper the `curly` rule uses, which matches the reporter's note that `curly` handles this case. Here the helper finds the inner `if` with no `else`, sees an `else` right after the block, and stops the report. To dig into the cause, compare 9.14.0's copy of the rule with the checkout's.

**Run:** `node repro/no-lonely-if-19033.js` uses the checkout and shows no behaviour change. To see the bug, install eslint@9.12.0 into `/tmp` and pass its path to the script; the full command is in the run command. The script exits with 1 when the fix changes how the code behaves.

**Artifacts:** repro/no-lonely-if-19033.js

I didn't change any production code; the only thing I added is the repro script.
